blogs.title: Airbnb regulations in Nice: what every owner should know in 2026
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Nice has recently adjusted its rules to limit the impact of short-term rentals. The maximum limit for short-term rental has been reduced to 90 days per year for primary residences.

content.introduction: Airbnb regulations in Nice have evolved significantly in 2026. Property owners must now navigate a strict legal framework to avoid penalties and optimize their short-term rental activity.

sections.title: A specific local rule on rental durations
sections.content:
The City of Nice has recently adjusted its rules to further limit the impact of short-term rentals on residential housing.

Primary residence: The maximum limit for short-term rental has been reduced to 90 days per year, down from 120 days previously for primary residences throughout the city. This restriction aims to preserve housing for residents while regulating tourist rentals.

 This rule applies everywhere in Nice since 2025/2026, even though it is particularly emphasized in the most stressed neighborhoods.

Secondary residence in certain high-demand areas: In areas where tourist pressure is strongest (Old Nice, Historic City Center, Riquier-Port-Mont-Boron, West Sector), quotas have been set: only 1.5% of primary residences in each of these sectors can obtain authorization for change of use.

In these same zones, authorization for change of use for a secondary residence is limited to 3 years, non-renewable.

sections.title: What this means for property owners
sections.content:
If the property is your primary residence, you must respect the limit of 90 nights of rental per year, even if you are only absent a few weeks during the year.

If the property is not your primary residence, in high-demand areas, you will need to:
- Obtain authorization for change of use to operate as tourist accommodation
- Comply with municipal quotas
- Plan the 3 years of authorization before any resale or strategy change

sections.title: Some useful regulatory reminders
sections.content:
Declaration at city hall and registration number: mandatory for any Airbnb listing, regardless of property status.

Tourist tax: collected and paid, even though Airbnb facilitates this process.

Penalties: fines can be significant in case of non-compliance - up to several thousand euros if the registration number is missing or if the day limit is exceeded.

sections.title: Why are regulations evolving?
sections.content: Nice faces strong real estate pressure. The municipality seeks to preserve the balance between residential housing, tourist activity, and economic dynamism. This will explains the progressive strengthening of controls and administrative obligations.

sections.title: How to secure your Airbnb activity in Nice?
sections.content:
The first step is to precisely analyze the legal situation of your property:
- Primary or secondary residence
- Condominium status
- Urban planning regulations
- Possible constraints from condominium regulations

A misinterpretation can compromise the project's profitability.

sections.title: Why reviews are crucial in Nice

The Airbnb algorithm favors listings:
- With excellent satisfaction rate

- With fast response rate

A traveler who feels they got a "good deal" more easily leaves a positive review.

- To send a personalized message before arrival

In Nice, many travelers arrive by train or plane. Smooth communication reduces travel stress.

sections.title: 4️Impeccable check-in

The first contact conditions the overall experience.

Organized welcome should include:

- A perfectly clean property

- A welcome booklet

A stay that starts without difficulty greatly increases chances of getting 5 stars.

sections.title: 5️Cleanliness: the non-negotiable criterion

On Airbnb, the "cleanliness" rating strongly influences the overall average.

In Nice, where sand and humidity can impact properties, professional cleaning between each stay is essential.

blogs.title: Airbnb or long-term rental in Nice: which option is the most profitable in 2026?
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Nice is one of the most attractive cities in France for real estate investors. For a property owner, the crucial question is often: Airbnb or long-term rental? Which option truly generates the best income?

content.introduction:
Nice is one of the most attractive cities in France for real estate investors. Between international tourism, professional events, and exceptional quality of life, rental demand remains strong year-round.

For a property owner, the crucial question is often: Airbnb or long-term rental? Which option truly generates the best income while remaining compliant with local regulations?

sections.title: Airbnb in Nice: opportunities and constraints
sections.content:
Advantages of short-term rental:
- Higher revenue: A city-center apartment can generate up to 3 to 5 times more than a traditional long-term rental.
- Flexibility: You can block certain periods for your personal use.
- Suited to international tourism: Foreign visitors primarily seek short stays.

Constraints to consider:
- Strict local rules: 90-day limit for primary residences and 3-year authorization for secondary residences in certain neighborhoods.
- Daily management: Responding to travelers, check-in/check-out, cleaning, linen, maintenance.
- Seasonality: High season is very lucrative, but low season requires an effective pricing strategy.

sections.title: Long-term rental: security and stability
sections.content:
Advantages:
- Regular and guaranteed income: Monthly rent ensures a stable cash flow.
- Fewer operational constraints: No frequent check-in/check-out, no cleaning between each stay.
- Administrative simplicity: Fewer declarations and daily monitoring.

Limitations:
- Capped revenue: Monthly rents are often lower than the potential income from a short-term rental.
- Less flexibility: A committed tenant limits personal use of the property.
- Tax impact: Taxation differs depending on the type of rental, with fewer optimization levers.

sections.title: Criteria for choosing the right option
sections.content:
1. Neighborhood and attractiveness: City center, Carré d'Or, or Old Nice are ideal for Airbnb. Less touristy areas are better suited for long-term rental.
2. Owner availability: Airbnb requires regular monitoring.
3. Financial goals: Maximize income or secure stable revenue.
4. Risk tolerance: Airbnb is more profitable but more variable.
5. Regulations: Respecting local quotas and limits is essential.

sections.title: How B&C Conciergerie helps owners decide
sections.content:
At B&C Conciergerie, we support each property owner with a personalized analysis of their property:

- Regulatory advice to stay compliant
- Personalized strategy based on your financial goals

Our approach allows you to choose the most profitable option while securing your investment.

faq.question: Is it profitable to switch to Airbnb with a property already in long-term rental?
faq.answer: Yes, but you need to optimize the listing, adjust pricing, and comply with regulations.

faq.question: Is Airbnb income reliable?
faq.answer: It is higher on average but more variable. Professional management reduces the risk.

faq.question: Can I combine both?
faq.answer: Yes. Some owners rent short-term during high season and long-term for the rest of the year.

faq.question: Can B&C Conciergerie manage this transition?
faq.answer: Yes, we support property owners at every step, from profitability calculations to complete management.
